Sixteen Branches, a Net-Zero Target, and a Leasehold Problem: What RS Locals Teaches Us About Embedded Energy Decisions

For a leased estate, some of the most important energy decisions happen before a retrofit is specified.

Pupsi Phull · Phull Insights22 September 20262 min readSustainable Performance
Evidence boundary

Personal analysis and professional reflection based on earlier postgraduate work. Named-company examples describe historical research, not current 2026 corporate policies, figures or commitments. No unpublished case result is represented as a verified outcome.

Why this matters

A national target does not tell a property team which site to renew, improve or leave. Lease terms and landlord permissions define what can be changed.

What the evidence suggests

The historical RS Locals study compared building types and low-carbon options as an academic exercise. The original site count, targets and portfolio assumptions reflect that period; they are not a statement about the company’s current estate or plans.

What it looks like in practice

Before selecting technology, a team should understand actual energy use, remaining lease term, building condition and who owns any improvement. Heating, lighting and on-site generation may each have a role, but the ordering depends on the site.

Practical next steps

Three things leaders can do now

01

Build a site-level energy and lease inventory.

02

Include energy performance and consent provisions in property negotiations.

03

Compare interventions against the expected occupancy period and maintenance responsibilities.
